title: The Faithful Betrayal
text:
Literary translation is often described as an act of faithful betrayal. The translator must convey not only the meaning of a text but also its rhythm, its ambiguities, and the cultural resonances that a native reader would instinctively perceive. Even a single metaphor can pose a dilemma: a literal rendering may sound awkward in the target language, while a domesticated version risks erasing the strangeness that made the original memorable.

Consequently, many translators regard their work less as a mechanical substitution of words than as a fresh interpretation. Some deliberately preserve foreign idioms to remind readers that they are encountering another culture, whereas others adapt them so thoroughly that the text reads as though it had been composed in the target language from the start. Neither approach is universally correct, and the choice often reveals the translator's underlying assumptions about the reader.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what must a literary translator convey besides the meaning of a text?
options: Its rhythm, ambiguities, and cultural resonances
The original page layout and typeface
The number of chapters in the book

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, why do some translators deliberately preserve foreign idioms?
options: To remind readers that they are encountering another culture
To make the text easier to translate back into the original language
Because the publisher requires it in every case
To shorten the text for a younger audience

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of translation?
options: Translation is closer to interpretation than to mechanical substitution
Translation should always be a word-for-word process
Translators have no influence on how readers understand a text
Only metaphors pose real problems for translators

questions.text: Why does the passage suggest that a translator's choice between approaches may be revealing?
options: It exposes what the translator assumes about the reader
It proves that one approach is always correct
It shows that the original author approved the translation
It indicates that the translator lacked skill in the target language

vocabulary.definition: loyal to the original, true to the source
associations or echoes of meaning that a word or idea carries
adapted so that it becomes familiar to the target audience
fixed phrases whose meaning cannot be understood from the individual words

paragraph_translations: A tradução literária costuma ser descrita como um ato de traição fiel. O tradutor deve transmitir não apenas o significado de um texto, mas também seu ritmo, suas ambiguidades e as ressonâncias culturais que um leitor nativo perceberia instintivamente. Até mesmo uma única metáfora pode representar um dilema: uma versão literal pode soar estranha na língua de chegada, enquanto uma versão domesticada corre o risco de apagar a estranheza que tornava o original memorável.

Consequentemente, muitos tradutores consideram seu trabalho menos uma substituição mecânica de palavras do que uma nova interpretação. Alguns preservam deliberadamente expressões idiomáticas estrangeiras para lembrar ao leitor que ele está entrando em contato com outra cultura, ao passo que outros as adaptam de forma tão completa que o texto parece ter sido escrito na língua de chegada desde o início. Nenhuma das abordagens é universalmente correta, e a escolha frequentemente revela os pressupostos do tradutor sobre o leitor.
